subject: POC kickoff: MAP action items for environment setup and gap closure
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@vertex-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@vertex-health.com>, Vertex Security <secops@vertex-health.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC planning — initial environment questions

Thanks Marissa — excited to get started. A couple of items from our side before the MAP call next week: 

- Org setup: we plan to create a dedicated org for the POC. Do you have a preferred naming convention (org ID / project) so we can mirror it?
- API keys: are there scoped key types for non-prod evaluation (rate limits / read-only tokens)?
- IP allowlist: we'll need exact IP ranges to open with our network team; can you share both egress and expected inbound IPs?

Also attaching a short spreadsheet with our internal owners. CC'ing SecOps for any compliance caveats.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Director, Platform Integrations
Vertex Health

Attachments: vertex-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet of internal owners)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@vertex-health.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC planning — initial environment questions

Thanks Marta — answered inline and added proposed milestones for the MAP kickoff call (see bullets). We can review on Wednesday.

- Org naming: recommend "vertex-poc-<env>-redwood" (e.g., vertex-poc-staging-redwood). We can accept any consistent ID, but please include "poc" to keep billing and observability separated.
- API keys: we'll provision evaluation-scoped keys with token-level quotas. Two types: 
  * eval_read (low-rate, read-only for embeddings and metadata)
  * eval_gen (higher rate, generation allowed; expires in 90 days)
  We will send a secure key delivery note and guidance for rotation.
- IP allowlist: typical inbound source IPs for our hosted route are 13.52.100.0/24 and 52.15.200.0/24; egress ranges depend on Dedicated v. Hosted routing (included in attachment api-key-instructions.txt). If you need VPC peering instead, we can start the peering paperwork.

Proposed MAP kickoff milestones (draft):
1) Week 0 (this week): org naming + owners assigned (Vertex) — owner: Marta
2) Week 1: eval API keys issued + quick smoke test — owner: Marissa / Aditya
3) Week 2: IP allowlist validated or VPC peering request submitted — owner: Jordan / Vertex SecOps
4) Week 3: Load test window + latency targets agreed — owners: Grace / Vertex Eng
5) Week 4: Acceptance criteria checklist + close decision meeting

I'll attach a VPC peering request template to expedite if you choose peering.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: api-key-instructions.txt, vpc-peering-request-template.yaml

From: Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@vertex-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@vertex-health.com>
Cc: Vertex Security <secops@vertex-health.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: clarifications on peering and IP strategy

Thanks all — quick clarification from SecOps: we prefer VPC peering for the appraisal workloads for two reasons: (1) we can control egress, (2) it avoids additional public allowlist maintenance.

Questions from our network team: 
- What is the expected ASN and the prefixes we should expect on the peering config?
- If peering is used, are there NAT gateways on your side or will traffic be sourced from our customer VPC subnets?

We can fill your peering template once we have ASN/prefix details. Goal: have peering request completed by Dec 18 to keep the MAP timeline.

—Tim
Tim Sanders
Network Lead, Vertex Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@vertex-health.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@vertex-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: clarifications on peering and IP strategy

Tim — good questions. Short answers below and I've attached the completed peering request fields we control.

- ASN & prefixes: our peering ASN is 64512. For peering we recommend the following prefixes to announce for the POC endpoint: 10.200.0.0/20 (control plane) and 10.201.0.0/20 (inference nodes).
- NAT gateways: for private peering we do not NAT on our side; traffic will be routed into our dedicated tenant subnets. If you need NATed egress, we can discuss a transit configuration but that will add latency.

Next steps I propose:
1) Vertex to complete the peering request with your VPC IDs and route table references (use our attached vpc-peering-request-template.yaml as the primary doc).
2) SecOps to review routing policy and confirm acceptance by Dec 18.
3) Once peering is accepted, Aditya will issue a time-boxed eval_gen key and coordinate a smoke test window (we suggest a 1-hour window for initial run).

I'll fill in the peering template fields we control and upload to the shared Drive.

Jordan Blake
Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-peering-request-template.yaml (template with filled fields for Redwood side)

From: Vertex Security <secops@vertex-health.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@vertex-health.com>, Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@vertex-health.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: peering policy and controls — security checklist

Jordan/Marissa — looping in our security checklist for any peering and API key exchange. Items we require before peering activation: 
- Mutual IDS/IPS expectations documented (we will share our monitoring hooks)
- Short-lived eval keys with enforced rotation (Aditya, confirm TTL configuration)
- Audit log exports for request/response headers during the smoke test window
- Acceptance of Redwood SOC2 Annex A (we'll send a signed NDA addendum if needed)

If Redwood can confirm the above and provide the audit log export method, we can aim to approve peering on Dec 28.

SecOps Team
Vertex Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@vertex-health.com>, Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@vertex-health.com>, Vertex Security <secops@vertex-health.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-28T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: MAP action items for environment setup and gap closure — confirmations and next steps

Thanks everyone — closing the loop before the holidays. From Redwood here: 

- Aditya confirms eval_gen keys will be time-boxed to 90 days with a 7-day rotation recommendation; TTL set to 90d for issuance and we will provide a key-rotation script in the shared Drive.
- Audit logs: we will enable request/response header export for the smoke test window and deliver a sample export to SecOps within 24 hours of the test.
- Peering: Jordan uploaded the filled template; we expect Vertex to return VPC IDs and route references by EOD Dec 30 so we can schedule the peer acceptance for Jan 4.

Action owners and dates (finalized):
- Marta: provide Vertex VPC IDs & route tables (due 2026-12-30)
- Vertex SecOps: review and sign peering controls & monitoring expectations (due 2026-12-28) — status: in review
- Aditya: provision eval keys and upload rotation script (due 2027-01-03)
- Grace: run smoke test and collect audit export (target window 2027-01-05 to 2027-01-06)
- Marissa: schedule acceptance call for Jan 7 to confirm close decision

If there are any gap items we haven't captured, reply inline. Otherwise I'll mark these in the MAP spreadsheet and update the HubSpot deal. Happy to jump on a short call over New Year if helpful.

Warmly,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
